proposals.title: ADR for hash function and packages/core implementation
proposals.why_now: ADR-009 explicitly requires the CanonicalEncoder to be specified in an ADR and implemented before any StateHash is computed. ADR-002 marks the hash function as DEFINIR and must be resolved via ADR before the RNG is implemented. packages/core is the foundation every other package depends on. The hash ADR and core implementation must come before any package that produces hashes or consumes the RNG.

proposals.title: ADR for rounding enforcement mechanism and blocking lint rule
proposals.why_now: ADR-004 states that calling division without an explicit rounding mode must be a compile-time error or blocking lint error, and marks the enforcement mechanism as DEFINIR. This must be resolved before any domain or world code is written, because once bare division appears in economic code it becomes a retroactive fix across many files. Resolving it now costs an ADR and a lint rule; resolving it in FASE-3 costs a multi-file audit.

proposals.title: packages/world price generator with two noise layers and two assets
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 requires the price generator with two noise layers (trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise) and two assets. This is the first functional deliverable of the simulation and the basis for INV-02 (direct price query equals tick-by-tick traversal) and INV-03 (player actions do not affect world price). Implementing it after core is established allows the team to validate the positionality guarantee early, before the full seven-asset configuration is added in FASE-2.

repository_assessment.current_state: Repository contains no implementation code. Only initialization files, the frozen specification, and empty benchmark history directories are present. No monorepo structure, no packages, no ADRs, no CI configuration, no Electron app, and no tests exist.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The monorepo itself does not exist. There is no TypeScript workspace, no package scaffold, and no build infrastructure, making it impossible to write or validate any code against the specification requirements.

warnings: Section 5.3 states bot wealth curves must be queryable in O(1) without tick-by-tick simulation, but also describes a grade-based simulation with liquidation evaluated at sampled price extremes. This is scoped to FASE-4 and does not block FASE-1, but the implementation strategy for bot liquidation on a coarse grid needs an ADR before FASE-4 begins, since the O(1) claim depends on the cache-per-block design being proven correct for the sampled-extreme liquidation approach.

Section 13 prohibits comments in pure packages, and section 16 item 7 requires ADRs for all DEFINIR resolutions. These two requirements are consistent with each other but the prohibition extends to code comments that would otherwise explain non-obvious invariants. Teams accustomed to inline documentation must structure all rationale in ADRs, not in code. This is not a contradiction but is a process risk if not established as a norm from the first commit.
